featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A charming little café tucked near Girgaon Chowpatty that works perfectly as a pit stop after a walk along Marine Drive. HAV Coffee has that relaxed neighbourhood café vibe — minimal interiors, the aroma of fresh coffee in the air, and a menu designed around comfort bites and specialty beverages.

The coffee selection is where the café shines. The Spanish Latte is easily one of the more enjoyable picks on the menu — creamy, slightly sweet and well balanced, making it ideal for those who prefer their coffee on the indulgent side. The Salted Caramel Cappuccino also stands out with a pleasant balance between sweetness and espresso bitterness. If you’re in the mood for something more dessert-like, the Lotus Biscoff Milkshake is rich and decadent, while their classic cold coffee is a refreshing companion for Mumbai’s warm evenings.

On the food front, the menu leans toward light café plates and quick bites. The Chilli Cheese Toast is simple but satisfying with a nice crisp base and gooey topping. The Korean Garlic Bun offers a buttery, garlicky bite that pairs well with coffee, while the Avocado on Toast feels fresh and wholesome. The Nachos with salsa and sour cream make for an easy sharing snack if you’re visiting with friends.

For something slightly more filling, the Mexican Burrito Bowl brings together beans, rice and toppings for a hearty café-style meal, while the Cottage Cheese Steak with ratatouille and Green Thai Curry with rice offer continental and Asian options that round out the menu nicely.

Overall, the food and drinks here lean above average, with the beverages being the highlight of the experience. The café works especially well as a relaxed coffee stop before or after spending time by the sea.

A pleasant spot for coffee lovers and casual café bites in this part of South Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited on a weekend evening. This place has a charming old heritage feel with a cozy complete 90s vibe, making it quite unique compared to modern cafés. Do note that parking is not available, so visiting on weekends may require some planning.

They serve pure vegetarian food along with egg-based dishes only (no other non-veg). Their egg akuri is one of the popular items, and it was quite good. The menu is limited but decent — we also tried pizza, which was very average. They serve good beer, which pairs nicely with the nostalgic vibe.

One of the highlights is the amazing jukebox with a great music selection that really enhances the retro atmosphere. The staff is polite and helpful, making the experience pleasant.

Important tip: they accept cash only, no online payment options, so remember to carry cash.

Overall, a great spot to visit with your gang if you enjoy 90s vibes,old pop music ,the Himesh and Imran Hashmi era music, simple comfort food, and chilled beer. A fun place to relax and spend quality time.
There is waiting time too but we got the table in few minutes.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Cafe De La Paix feels less like entering a restaurant and more like walking into a living piece of Mumbai’s history. In a city that is constantly reinventing itself, this beautiful 90+ year-old Irani café stands as a reminder of a slower, more charming era.
The menu is delightfully simple yet comforting. We started with the classic Irani chai and brun maska—a combination that never goes out of style. The chai was rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced, while the brun maska was crisp on the outside, soft within, and generously buttered.
The breakfast offerings are equally satisfying. Whether you prefer a full fry, half fry, plain omelette, masala omelette, or cheese omelette, there’s something deeply nostalgic about watching these timeless dishes being prepared and served without any unnecessary frills. The Akuri was beautifully spiced and creamy, while the Sali Par Eedu showcased the comforting simplicity that Parsi cuisine does so well. The Special Maggi was surprisingly delicious and a must-try, and the kheema preparations remain a favourite among regulars for good reason.
What truly elevates the experience, however, is not just the food but the atmosphere. The vintage interiors, old-world furniture, framed memories on the walls, and the unmistakable charm of a classic Irani café create an ambience that is impossible to replicate. Every corner tells a story.
A special mention for Gustad Irani, whose warmth and hospitality make the experience even more memorable. He was incredibly welcoming, happy to chat, and added a personal touch that made us feel less like customers and more like guests. Conversations with him are as much a part of the Cafe De La Paix experience as the chai itself.
The food is good, but the real attraction is the heritage, the history, and the soul of the place. One of the few surviving Irani cafés in South Mumbai, Cafe De La Paix is not merely somewhere to eat it’s somewhere to pause, soak in the nostalgia, and appreciate a treasured piece of the city’s cultural fabric.
A timeless Mumbai gem that deserves to be cherished and visited again and again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Slice of Soul in Mumbai – Food, Warmth, and a Wagging Tail at Café De La Paix

Tucked away in the heart of Bombay, Café De La Paix is more than just a café — it’s an experience. Run single-handedly by the incredibly passionate Mr. Ustaad, this place is built on love, flavour, and an unshakable commitment to doing things right.

We had the absolutely comforting Mutton Kheema Pav with two perfectly half-fried eggs, and the unforgettable Chicken Sully Boty with soft pav — a Parsi-inspired masterpiece with just the right punch. Add to that their special Bun Muskan, nostalgic chai (1 by 2), rich coffee, and an ice cream soda that instantly took us back to simpler times — every item served was filled with soul.

But what makes this café truly special is the man behind it all: Mr. Ustaad — the chef, the owner, the one who personally selects every raw ingredient, cooks every dish with patience, and ensures quality like no other. He has one humble helper who not only serves the food but also keeps the place spotless — every inch of the café feels like it’s cleaned and cared for with genuine affection.

And just when you think it couldn’t get better, Cherry, the café’s charming resident dog, walks in and plops himself under your table. He plays with you, rests his head on your feet, and wraps you in a cozy, warm presence that no café can ever replicate.

Café De La Paix is a true Bombay gem — simple, soulful, and full of heart. Salute to Mr. Ustaad for creating magic with his two hands and an open heart. We’ll definitely be coming back, not just for the food, but for the feeling.
